newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialist proposes France Telecom criteria.
newsitem.headline: French Socialist proposes France Telecom criteria.

text.p: A senior Socialist parliamentarian suggested three criterion on Friday to be used by the state in determining whether to go ahead with the privatisation of France Telecom.

"If we can provide employees with work guarantees, enable France Telecom to reach cooperation agreements -- notably with other European operators, and if we can use the money that is taken in for jobs for young people, let's take a look," deputy Claude Bartolone told reporters.
"But if someone tells us all of a sudden that we are doing this without an industrial strategy, then why go ahead," he said.

Bartolone acknowledged that certain France Telecom employees feared privatisation but also were aware "that they must reach agreements with European firms if they don't want to see the Americans come in."
The previous rightist government's planned privatisation of the state telecommunications company has been put on ice by France's new leftist government, which took power last month.
Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Thursday that Paris should be flexible about privatising state enterprises and not turn its back on industrial reality for the sake of ideology.

In his first television interview since taking office a month ago, Jospin renewed a pledge to consult the personnel of France Telecom before any decision to sell shares. ((-- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5339))
